author: frontier (Claude Opus 5.5, the orchestrating session), 2026-10-22
authorNote: Written by the same session that wrote the gameqa-web build and its injected bugs, after the bugs. It is meant to be game-agnostic (derived from research/landscape-20261006/08-worked-example-ai-game-qa.md section 4-5: check ladder, personas, repro and minimize), but its author knew the bugs: a leakage path. The same QA heuristics text is given to the solo-agent arm, so the agent-vs-workflow comparison varies structure, not knowledge.
purpose: Exploratory QA of a game build exposed through a deterministic test API: a cheap model instantiates personas and executable checks from the design document, code plays the personas' plans and evaluates every check on every tick, code reproduces and delta-debugs each violation to a 1-minimal repro, and a cheap model judges each minimized candidate against the document before it becomes a report.

inputs.env: a session with reset(seed), run(tokens) -> per-tick observations

nodes.verify: code: every check parses in the check language; rejected checks go back once with the parser errors (node construct-repair)

reads: known violations (check ids and rules only)

body.does: run each plan from a fresh game; evaluate the generic detectors and every check on every tick; record the first violation per check with its seed and token prefix

nodes.does: one candidate per signature (the check and the screen it was violated on: the open dialog, else the mode), the shortest prefix seen; checks that error are dropped; at most maxCandidates, taken breadth first across checks (1.1.0: was one candidate per check, which capped the findings of a check that catches different faults on different screens)
replay each candidate twice from a fresh game; keep it only if the same check is violated both times (determinism class D0)
ddmin over the token list with the predicate 'the same check is violated on the same screen' (plus a single-token removal pass), so every kept repro is 1-minimal for its signature

reads: candidate: check rule and expressions, minimized tokens, the full trace of the minimized replay
nodes.returns: {verdicts[] of {candidate, is_bug, bug_class, title, observed, expected}}
nodes.note: the false-alarm filter: a violated check can be a wrong check (e.g. behaviour the document marks by design)

nodes.does: emit one report per candidate judged a bug, with the minimized tokens and seed

genericDetectors.rule: a script error is shown by the page
the observable state does not change for 30 ticks and no dialog or button is visible

personaArchetypes: completionist mapper: visits every area and collects everything, finishes the level
sequence-breaker: tries to reach places or outcomes early or by unintended routes
chaos tester: pauses, restarts, quits and presses several keys during transitions (collecting, getting hurt, finishing), spams input
literal newcomer: follows the document step by step and checks each sentence literally
economy auditor: drives counters (score, lives, items, timers) to their limits and checks every amount
photographer: opens every dialog and menu and checks what is shown and what can be clicked
heuristics: Turn every rule in the design document into something you can observe: amounts, limits, caps and counts; 'never', 'always', 'only' and 'at most' statements; what may change in each mode (playing, paused, a dialog open); and what the display must show.
Compare what is displayed (HUD text, dialogs, buttons) with the underlying state on every step: a display that disagrees with the state is a bug.

Probe boundaries and transitions: values near zero and near limits; acting at the moment something happens (pausing, collecting, getting hurt, finishing); several inputs in the same tick; repeating an action; actions in unusual modes.
Exercise every control in every mode, including dialog buttons, and check that each visible button can be clicked.
Go deep as well as wide: finish the level, use every mechanic, reach every area; some bugs need large values or only appear late.
Behaviour the document marks 'by design' is not a bug.
Before reporting, confirm the bug by replaying from a fresh game, then cut the token list down until removing any single token makes the bug disappear.
checkLanguage: Checks are written in a small expression language (a JavaScript subset), evaluated after every tick with: cur = the observation after this tick {token, click, state, hud, ui, errors}; prev = the observation before this tick (for the first tick: the fresh game); step = the tick index. state is the game's test API state (field names as in the design document); hud.<field> is the displayed text of a HUD field (for this test API: score, lives, keys, coins, time, dash, e.g. hud.score is the text shown for the score); ui is a list of {id, kind ('dialog'|'button'|'toast'|'text'), visible, text, rect, top (buttons only: whether a click at its centre reaches it)}. Operators: . [] ! - * / % + < <= > >= == != && || ?: (== compares values deeply, so objects and lists can be compared). Functions: abs min max floor round sign len includes(listOrText, value) num(text) (the first integer in a text, NaN if none) str(value) tile(obs, x, y) (the map character at x,y in that observation) any(list, x => expr) all(list, x => expr) count(list, x => expr) find(list, x => expr). Reading a missing field gives undefined (no error). A check is {id, rule (quote or paraphrase the design sentence it enforces), bug_class, when (optional: check only ticks where this is true), expect (must be true on every such tick)}. Write checks that are true on every tick of a correct game, including respawns, restarts, dialogs and pauses: guard with when where the rule applies only sometimes.

checkExamples.rule: Fuel never exceeds the tank size.
While docked the ship does not move.
The gauge shows the current fuel.
